Brassil Legal Reporter Photographer: Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg Documents Third Circuit Docket Related Stories Prediction Market Law Keeps Veering, Inviting Supreme Court (1) Aug. 31, 2026, 7:46â¯PM UTC Kalshi Takes Hit as Appeals Court Says Sports Bets Not Swaps (5) Aug. 28, 2026, 5:17â¯PM UTC Prediction Markets Get Cold Reception Before Ninth Circuit (1) April 16, 2026, 8:24â¯PM UTC Kalshi Stays Free of New Jersey Regs With Appeals Court Win (2) April 6, 2026, 2:20â¯PM UTC Search by Law Firm Milbank LLP Search by Topic derivatives market preliminary injunctions subject matter jurisdiction swaps preemption gambling regulation Search by Company Robinhood Markets Inc The US Supreme Court has the opportunity to clear up a nationwide legal debate over whether sports prediction markets offer wagering or derivatives trading, with New Jersey regulators Wednesday imploring justices to take up their spat with Kalshi Inc. New Jersey seeks high court review of an appellate ruling favoring the prediction market provider. The petition comes a week after another circuit split on whether these offerings are sports bets, subject to state regulation, or hedging tools called âswapsâ that are under the purview of a Trump administration thatâs aggressively asserted it has sole oversight. WATCH: Betting on Sports Is Legal. But Are Prediction Markets Like Kalshi and Polymarket Different? âCompanies like Kalshi claim to offer legal sports betting in all 50 States, but they refuse to follow the gambling laws of any State,â Attorney General Jennifer Davenport said in an emailed statement about the filing of the petition. âThese companies have no right to offer their sports bets without following state law, which is why dozens of States across the ideological spectrum have opposed them.â The petition said prediction market providers offering sports bets have dragged at least 20 states into litigation, generating a âdirect, acknowledged, and irreconcilable split between the Third and Ninth Circuits. âThat split has tremendous importance, as it will determine whether a multi-billion-dollar gaming industry can suddenly operate free from state sports-gaming laws,â it said. âWe disagree with New Jerseyâs filing,â Dani Lever, a Kalshi spokeswoman, said in an emailed statement. âKalshi is an open, nationwide financial exchange. It cannot be regulated by 50 different regulators.â The US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, in a 2-1 April decision , said Kalshi was likely to succeed with its argument that the federal Commodity Exchange Act preempts state gaming laws. Kalshiâs sports event contracts were swaps traded on federally-designated contract market, meaning the Commodity Futures Trading Commission has exclusive jurisdiction over them, Judge David J.Porter wrote for the majority. Judge Michael A. Chagares joined him in upholding a preliminary injunction against New Jersey gambling regulators. It was the first circuit court to weigh in on the widespread legal fight for regulatory control of the multibillion-dollar industry. Then the Ninth Circuit last week unanimously said that Kalshiâs sports event contracts were bets, not swaps, affirming a lower courtâs decision to dissolve a preliminary injunction that had shielded the company. âBoth the Third Circuit and the District of New Jersey sided with Kalshi because the CFTCâs exclusive jurisdiction preempts state law,â Kalshiâs Lever said. âWhile New Jersey points to a recent decision in the Ninth Circuit, that decision agreed with that key principle. Where it differed, it did so based on a regulation thatâs in the process of being rewritten. We remain confident in the lower courtsâ rulings, and nothing in New Jerseyâs filing today changes our view.â Swaps or Not Prediction markets such as Kalshiâs let users put money on a range of yes-no outcomes â for example, if Attorney General Ken Paxton (R-Texas) will win his Senate race or if Purdue will win Fridayâs college football matchup. States argue these platforms offer glorified sports betting, providing unlicensed wagering in violation of their laws. Kalshi, Crypto.com , and Robinhood Markets Inc. are among those trying to fend off state gaming officials in the nationwide dispute mainly centered around sports prediction markets. The Trump administrationâs CFTC has aggressively touted that it has exclusive jurisdiction over these designated contract markets. President Donald Trump has familial ties to the industry. After the 2008 financial crisis, Congress added and defined swaps in the CEA. âAt issue is whether Congress federalized a multi-billion-dollar sports-betting industry via a single word and its definition â âswapâ â in Dodd-Frank. After all, if Kalshi is right that it can offer sports bets on federal exchanges irrespective of state law, companies can disregard all state sports-gambling statutes with ease, so long as they register with the CFTC,â said New Jerseyâs petition. Dissenting from the Third Circuit majority, Judge Jane R. Roth disputed that sports event contracts fall solely within the CFTCâs ambit, calling them âvirtually indistinguishableâ from sportsbook products. Roth said New Jerseyâs laws seemed to complement the CEA. Milbank LLP represents Kalshi. The case is Flaherty v. KalshiEX LLC , U.S., cert petition filed 9/2/26.
